answer: Sybil resistance comes from making identity cost continuous, not one-time. Every agent must stake and keep doing verifiable work, and new identities enter only through a guarantee thread from already-trusted agents. The real defense is detecting hollow nodes: sybil clusters act minimally, never interact with outsiders, and never govern — like an empty walnut shell with no kernel. Graph analysis spots these low-connection, low-contribution nodes and thins their voting weight, so forging a crowd costs more than any gain.
